title: Data export scoping sync, Oct 14
excerpt: For Compliance, "customer data" has to include derived and analytics data, not just the profile fields.

title: #data-export thread
excerpt: Following up on the sync: a data subject request covers derived and analytics data too, so a profile-only export would not satisfy it.

title: Privacy Policy v3
excerpt: "Customer data" covers all data we hold about a customer, including derived analytics.

title: Data export scoping sync, Oct 14
excerpt: The estimate swings a lot. Profile data only is about one sprint. Adding derived and analytics data is closer to four, because those tables live in the warehouse and have no per-customer export path today.

title: Data export scoping sync, Oct 14
excerpt: Okay. We hold the estimate, Leo sizes both scopes, and Sana and I come back with one definition.

title: #data-export thread
excerpt: Sized both scopes. Profile fields only: about 1 sprint. Profile plus derived and analytics data: about 4 sprints, mostly warehouse work.

title: Data Export PRD v2
excerpt: In scope: profile fields (name, email, plan, preferences). Out of scope: derived or analytics data.

title: Data export scoping sync, Oct 14
excerpt: Privacy Policy v3 is explicit on this. It says customer data covers all data we hold about a customer, including derived analytics.

title: #data-export thread
excerpt: Agreed with Maya: if profile fields ship first, the release is labeled a partial export and can't be used to answer data subject requests. The full definition is still open.

title: Data export scoping sync, Oct 14
excerpt: A partial export can be fine as a first release, but we can't call it complete, and it can't be how we answer a data subject request.

title: Identity checks pilot readiness, Oct 19
excerpt: Our tolerance for false positives is two percent. Above that, too many legitimate customers land in manual review and we can't clear the queue.

title: Risk Policy v4
excerpt: Automated identity checks must keep the false-positive rate at or below 2%.

title: KYC Vendor Integration Spec v1
excerpt: Target false-positive threshold: 5%. Retain ID document images for 24 months.

title: Identity checks pilot readiness, Oct 19
excerpt: Hold on, we built to five percent. That's the number in the vendor integration spec, version one.

title: #kyc-pilot thread
excerpt: Confirmed in staging config: the match threshold is set to 5%. Getting to 2% needs the vendor to retrain the model, estimate is two weeks.

title: Identity checks pilot readiness, Oct 19
excerpt: Separate concern. The integration keeps ID document images for 24 months. Our retention standard says 90 days for government ID images.

title: Security Data Retention Standard v2
excerpt: Government ID images must be deleted within 90 days of verification unless a documented exception is approved.

title: Identity checks pilot readiness, Oct 19
excerpt: We use those images to review appeals and tune the fraud rules. Ninety days is shorter than most of our appeal cases.

title: #kyc-pilot thread
excerpt: Most appeals close within 18 months, and we retune fraud rules against the same images, so Risk is asking for 24 months of retention.

title: Identity checks pilot readiness, Oct 19
excerpt: So two outcomes. The pilot is on hold until Eng retunes to two percent, and Amir and Dana bring back a retention proposal.

title: #kyc-pilot thread
excerpt: Risk won't sign off on the pilot above 2%. The pilot stays on hold until the retuned test run is in.

title: Enterprise SSO kickoff, Oct 21
excerpt: Security's position is that MFA is required for every account that signs in to an enterprise workspace, admins especially.

title: Enterprise Security Baseline v2
excerpt: All accounts signing in to an enterprise workspace must use multi-factor authentication.

title: Enterprise SSO kickoff, Oct 21
excerpt: If we force MFA on day one we hurt trials. Growth needs signup to stay frictionless, with a new user in the product in under a minute.

title: Growth Q4 Plan
excerpt: Target: a new trial user reaches the product in under 60 seconds, with no extra verification steps at signup.

title: Enterprise SSO kickoff, Oct 21
excerpt: Then for now MFA is optional during trials, and we revisit it after the pen test.

title: #sso-rollout thread
excerpt: Decision from today's kickoff: MFA is optional during trials. We revisit after the pen test.

title: Enterprise SSO: pen test review, Oct 28
excerpt: The testers got into a trial workspace with a reused password and invited themselves as admin. Trial workspaces connected to SSO hold real customer directory data.

title: Pen Test Report, Oct 2026
excerpt: Finding 3 (high): a trial workspace connected to SSO was accessed with a reused password because MFA was not enforced.

title: Enterprise SSO: pen test review, Oct 28
excerpt: Decision: MFA is required before any workspace enables SSO, trials included. This replaces last week's decision.

title: #sso-rollout thread
excerpt: Update: MFA is now required before any workspace enables SSO, trials included. This replaces the Oct 21 decision.
